title: heap-use-after-free in sqlite3DbFreeNN
live_proof: the defect is public and fixed upstream in 3.29.0, after the 3.22.0 pin; sqlite3_blob_close in the pinned tree finalizes before freeing the Incrblob, so the last statement on a zombie connection frees the connection and sqlite3DbFree then reads it. Host ASan on this case source: heap-use-after-free, 696 bytes inside a 704-byte region, read in sqlite3DbFreeNN <- sqlite3DbFree <- sqlite3_blob_close, freed by sqlite3LeaveMutexAndCloseZombie <- sqlite3_finalize <- sqlite3_blob_close, allocated by openDatabase (results/2026-10-11-host-asan)
object: the sqlite3 connection itself, allocated by openDatabase: sqlite3DbFree reads db->lookaside on it, not the Incrblob it is freeing
lifetime_ender: sqlite3_close_v2 makes the connection a zombie, and the sqlite3_finalize inside sqlite3_blob_close then frees it (sqlite3LeaveMutexAndCloseZombie) before the same function reads it again
fidelity: real consumer, real allocator: SQLite's own memsys5 heap. Lookaside is OFF in this corpus (-DSQLITE_DEFAULT_LOOKASIDE=0,0), so the Incrblob comes straight from memsys5 and the case prints sqlite3_db_status to say so; the stale read is of the connection's own lookaside descriptor field, which sqlite3DbFree consults whether or not a pool exists, and host ASan confirms it fires with lookaside on and off. Ported 2026-10-05 from the legacy standalone domain onto REPRO322_MAIN, which is what let the Sublet arm run it at all

fault_sites_why: sqlite3_blob_close frees the lookaside-allocated Incrblob through sqlite3DbFree after sqlite3_close_v2 freed the connection and its lookaside pool, so the stale reads are sqlite3DbFreeNN's (consumer; PROVENANCE.md).
